Thai king and queen visit Hanoi university that hosts Thai language, culture center
picked.body: As part of their state visit to Vietnam, Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua and Queen Suthida visit Hanoi University on Wednesday afternoon. Vietnam-Thailand ties are on clear display at Hanoi University through Thai language training, cultural exchanges and student exchange programs. The university's Thai Language and Culture Center was established in 2009. King Maha Vajiralongkorn and Queen Suthida watch a dance performance by students. The king and queen applaud a dance performed to the song "Rak Thai" (Love Thailand). A student representative extends best wishes to the king and queen. More than 1,000 students at the university have studied Thai as a second foreign language, nearly 200 learners have taken short-term Thai courses, and nearly 150 students have studied or joined exchange programs in Thailand. Hanoi University President Nguyen Van Trao says it is an honor to host the king and queen, calling the visit a source of encouragement for the lecturers, staff and students who teach, work and study there. The king and queen tour the Thai Language and Culture Center. The university's Thai Cultural Space is a highlight of cultural and educational cooperation between the two countries. Renovated and expanded in 2018 with support from the Thai Embassy in Hanoi, the space lets Vietnamese students learn about and experience Thai culture through language, art and interactive activities. The king and queen watch students make handicrafts. The king and queen present teaching materials and equipment to the Thai Language and Culture Center. Hanoi University's leadership says the school will build on its strengths in foreign language training, international education, cultural exchange and academic cooperation, while creating more opportunities for students from both countries to learn, share experiences and grow together, helping nurture Vietnam-Thailand friendship among the younger generation.

picked.t: Vietnamese woman arrested for stealing Chinese tourist's luggage at Bangkok airport
picked.body: The suspect, identified as Ong, was detained by Tourist Police, airport security, and officers from Suvarnabhumi Airport Police Station under an arrest warrant issued by the Samut Prakan Provincial Court on charges of airport theft. The theft was discovered around 8:00 p.m. on Sept. 7, 2026, after Chinese tourist Qin Yusong landed on flight GX8907 and discovered his pink Rimowa suitcase was missing from conveyor belt number 15, Thai news site Daily News reported. Qin lodged a complaint at the airport police station, reporting that the luggage held cash, personal items, and a luxury wristwatch valued at more than 200,000 yuan (US$30,000). Surveillance footage reviewed by investigators identified a Vietnamese passenger, who had arrived from Ho Chi Minh City on the same day, taking the luggage from the carousel. Police tracked the woman as she departed the airport by taxi, moved between several hotels in Bangkok’s Huai Khwang District, and later relocated to Bo Win District in Chon Buri, as reported by Thaiger . Authorities maintained surveillance on her movements until Sept. 15, intercepting and arresting her outside a residential mansion in the Sukhumvit area after presenting the court warrant. During questioning, the suspect admitted to taking the suitcase and revealed she had stored it at a condominium unit in Huai Khwang. Officers searched the property, successfully recovered the pink Rimowa luggage along with the reported valuables inside, and transferred the suspect to investigators to proceed with legal action.
